result.title: AttnSR: Attention Step Reward for Long-Horizon Agentic RL
result.comment: 20 pages, 4 figures, including appendices. Code: https://github.com/fairyshine/AttnSR
result.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents make multi-step decisions, yet outcome-reward-only reinforcement learning provides little direct supervision for individual steps. We introduce AttnSR, a step-level reward augmentation method that derives reward allocations from policy attention extracted during training replay, without a separately trained reward model or additional rollouts. AttnSR traces backward through the policy model attention graph to estimate the relevance of earlier steps to the final response. The terminal step, measured relative to a running baseline, determines whether these rewards reinforce or penalize the selected steps. In a controlled Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct study, AttnSR consistently outperforms the PPO baseline across all evaluated checkpoints on ALFWorld, raising final held-out success from 91.2% to 97.1%. The ablation experiment shows that the benefit depends on how intermediate rewards are assigned, rather than simple accumulation of step rewards over time. AttnSR also improves ScienceWorld at every checkpoint while cutting environment interactions by 29.9%. These results support policy attention as a practical prior for step-level reward allocation in long-horizon agentic RL. Code is available at https://github.com/fairyshine/AttnSR .

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AttnSR：在长程 LLM agent 的 RL 训练中，训练回放时回溯策略模型的 attention 图来估计各中间步对最终回答的相关性，并以此做步级奖励分配，无需额外奖励模型或 rollout；在 ALFWorld、ScienceWorld 上优于 PPO 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用 attention 图回溯估计步级贡献的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中哪些视觉或 latent 推理步真正影响最终答案这一贡献分配与监督问题，但该工作面向纯文本 agent 任务，能否迁移到多模态内部状态尚不确定。
